subject: System Design
title: Key-Value Stores
description: A micro-lesson that makes Key-Value Stores usable.

hook.text: Given a key, return its value. That's it. Key-value stores are the simplest databases possible.

buildup.text: Redis and DynamoDB store data as key-value pairs. Lookups by key are O(1) — constant time.

discovery.text: They excel at caching, session storage, and real-time counters where lookup speed is critical.

twist.text: You can only query by key. Need to search by value or range? A key-value store can't help you.

climax.text: Key-value stores are powerful for simple access patterns but useless for complex queries.

punchline.text: Blazing fast if you know the key. Useless if you don't.

quiz.question: What is the main limitation of key-value stores?
options: You can only query by key, not by value or range
